headline: Australian inflation came in hotter than expected today, putting a September RBA rate hike firmly back on the table — meanwhile gold hits three-month highs as Iran tensions keep markets on edge.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a solid session today, jumping 2.9% to $5.29. No single catalyst in the news, but lithium stocks got a bounce — possibly short-covering or speculative buying ahead of any signs of a demand recovery. The broader lithium picture remains tough though, with carbonate prices still under pressure and a 2027 supply surplus looming.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a good session today, up 0.86% to $93.61. Emerging markets got a lift partly from the stronger Aussie dollar (up 0.37% to US71.8c) and generally positive sentiment out of Asia. Still sitting just fractionally below your cost base — nothing to worry about for a long-term hold.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 0.9% last night to US$491.71, continuing a strong run — up roughly 28% over the past month. Analysts are pointing to robust cloud demand and the AI story, with some now eyeing a path to $600. The long-term thesis here looks very healthy.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI edged up 0.19% today to $16.09 — a small positive move in a generally mixed session for tech. This ETF is still carrying a paper loss of about $44 (down ~15% overall), but today's nudge higher is consistent with the broader AI sector holding up. Long-term story unchanged.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today — up just one cent to $77.22. The ASX 200 dipped 0.4% on the hot inflation print, but VDHG's global diversification cushioned that. Essentially flat and steady — exactly what you'd expect from a diversified fund on a nervy local day.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped a modest 0.36% last night to US$343.34 — essentially noise. The underlying story remains strong: Alphabet recently reported a 24% earnings rise, and CEO Sundar Pichai says Google's AI products (like AI Overviews) now reach over 2.5 billion monthly users, which is a huge positive for ad revenue long-term.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 0.48% today to $525.98 in AUD terms. This reflects the ASX pricing of the US market from last night, slightly dragged by the stronger Aussie dollar (which makes USD-denominated assets worth a little less in AUD). The US market itself (S&P 500) was actually up last night — this is a currency effect more than anything.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two barely moved last night, down just 0.24% to US$232.93. There's been a flurry of GTA 6 leak news — a big 'Cyberleak' has been doing the rounds, with reports that Take-Two lawyers even showed up at a leaker's home. This kind of pre-release buzz is generally more noise than signal for the stock. Long-term GTA 6 launch story intact.

watch_today.title: Hot inflation data puts September RBA rate hike back in play
watch_today.detail: Australia's latest inflation print came in above forecasts today, reigniting fears the Reserve Bank (RBA) will lift interest rates again at its September meeting. Higher rates are bad for growth stocks and property, and would put pressure on consumer spending. Keep an eye on any RBA commentary this week — this is the biggest local macro story right now.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — good day, but the lithium recovery is still fragile
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced 2.9% today to $5.29, which is encouraging. But lithium carbonate prices recently fell another 10.3% and analysts are flagging a potential 2027 supply surplus. You're still down about 21.5% on this position overall. The bounce is nice but doesn't change the long-term picture yet — sit tight and watch whether this is the start of a real trend reversal.

watch_today.title: MSFT — strong run, long-term thesis very much intact
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is up ~28% in the past month and rose another 0.9% last night to US$491.71. Cloud demand and AI tailwinds are the drivers, with analysts now debating a path to $600. You're up nearly 11% on this position. No reason to change anything — this is a long-term hold doing exactly what it should.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — small bounce, still in the red overall
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF crept up 0.19% today to $16.09, but you're still sitting on a paper loss of about $44 (down ~15%). Apple just announced new M6 chips with big AI compute leaps, and AI sector news remains busy. The long-term AI theme is strong — this is a hold, and dips could be top-up territory if you believe in the theme.

watch_today.title: Gold surging — good backdrop for defensive holdings
watch_today.detail: Gold hit a three-month high last night, up 1.12% to US$4,689. The drivers are Iran war fears and uncertainty around Trump's economic policies. This is a 'risk-off' signal (investors moving to safety) — worth watching as it could weigh on growth stocks in coming days if tensions escalate further.

watch_today.title: VGE.AX — a rare green day, long-term still slightly underwater
watch_today.detail: VGE rose 0.86% today to $93.61, helped by the stronger AUD and positive emerging markets sentiment. You're just $1.41 in the red overall — basically breakeven. Nothing to act on, just a quiet positive session.

world.summary: The big global stories today centre on US domestic politics — particularly a major Supreme Court ruling on mail-in voting that threatens upcoming midterms — along with the ongoing Iran conflict's economic ripple effects and gold hitting three-month highs.

stories.title: US Supreme Court backs Trump mail-voting restrictions ahead of midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The US Supreme Court has cleared the way for Trump's executive order restricting mail-in ballots, dealing a major blow to Democratic voting rights efforts ahead of the midterm elections. A lower court had previously blocked the order, but the Supreme Court's decision to let it proceed means millions of Americans who rely on postal voting could face new hurdles. Critics argue this is a deliberate attempt to suppress votes in key states; supporters say it's about election integrity. This is one of the biggest threats to the democratic process in the US ahead of the midterms.

stories.title: Trump administration targets James Comey and others in political campaign
stories.why_it_matters: ABC News has published a full list of individuals targeted by the Trump administration in what critics are calling a politically motivated campaign — including former FBI Director James Comey. The move involves using government agencies and legal mechanisms to go after perceived political opponents. This escalating pattern of using executive power against individuals is raising serious concerns about rule of law in the United States, with implications for institutional stability that global investors are watching closely.

stories.title: US starts returning staff to Middle East missions after Iran war evacuations
stories.why_it_matters: The US has begun returning diplomatic staff to its Middle East embassies and missions after evacuating them during the Iran conflict — a tentative signal that the immediate military crisis may be de-escalating. However, Iran has vowed to respond to fresh US sanctions, and oil markets remain volatile. The US military and diplomatic posture in the region is still on high alert, and any flashpoint could re-escalate quickly. This matters for oil prices, global supply chains, and market confidence.

stories.title: Gold hits three-month high on Iran war fears and Trump economic uncertainty
stories.why_it_matters: Gold surged to a three-month high last night, climbing 1.12% to US$4,689 an ounce. The Guardian reports the rally is being driven by two things: ongoing fears about the Iran conflict's economic fallout, and deep uncertainty about Trump's economic management. When investors get nervous, they pile into gold as a 'safe haven.' The fact that gold is at multi-month highs tells you that a lot of smart money is still very worried about what's coming.

stories.title: US farmers facing worst crisis in decades as war sends costs spiralling
stories.why_it_matters: American farmers are facing their worst financial crisis in decades, with the Iran war sending fuel, fertiliser, and transport costs through the roof while export markets are disrupted by sanctions and supply chain chaos. The AFR reports farmers are being squeezed from both sides — higher costs and lower prices for their goods. This has knock-on effects for global food prices, which are already elevated, and could add to inflationary pressures felt here in Australia at the supermarket.

markets.summary: Last night the US market held up reasonably well — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both pushed higher, helped by the tech sector. But back home, the ASX 200 had a rough day after the hot inflation print spooked investors. Oil slid nearly 3%, while gold continued its impressive run to three-month highs.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Dropped today after inflation came in above forecasts, raising fears of another RBA rate hike in September.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Edged up last night — US markets relatively calm despite geopolitical noise.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech led US gains last night, with Microsoft and AI-related names doing the heavy lifting.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell sharply last night — down nearly 3% — as reports of the US returning staff to Middle East missions hinted at slight de-escalation of Iran tensions.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged to a three-month high, driven by Iran war fears and uncertainty about Trump's economic policies. Investors are seeking safety.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar strengthened slightly today. Ironically, the hot inflation data supports the case for higher rates, which tends to attract foreign capital — pushing the AUD up a little.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Australia's inflation coming in hotter than expected, putting the RBA in a very tight spot ahead of its September meeting. Separately, PM Albanese is trying to manage growing pushback on his AI data centre plans.

stories.title: Inflation lands above forecasts — September RBA rate hike now a real chance
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's latest inflation figures dropped today and they were worse than economists predicted — ABC News called it an 'unfortunate kick in the guts.' The hotter-than-expected read has sent markets scrambling to price in a higher chance of the Reserve Bank raising interest rates at its September board meeting. Higher rates mean more expensive mortgages, tighter household budgets, and generally bad news for growth stocks. The ASX 200 fell 0.4% today in direct response. Watch the RBA closely — their September decision is now a live event.

stories.title: Albanese moves to calm data centre concerns as climate experts urge tighter rules
stories.why_it_matters: PM Albanese is facing a growing chorus of concern over his government's push to build large AI data centres across Australia. Critics — including climate experts — say the rules governing these energy-hungry facilities are insufficient, warning 'we've got one shot to get the rules right.' Meanwhile, a separate AAP report describes the plan as 'heavy-handed.' The government is trying to position Australia as an AI infrastructure hub, but the environmental and regulatory debate is heating up.

stories.title: 50,000 Australians sign petition calling for a Human Rights Act
stories.why_it_matters: A petition backed by Amnesty International has hit 50,000 signatures calling on the Australian government to introduce a Human Rights Act — something Australia currently lacks, making it one of the few democracies without such a law. Supporters argue it would protect Australians from government overreach. The Albanese government has yet to commit, and the petition is likely designed to pressure them ahead of the next parliamentary term.

stories.title: RBA signals higher rates working, but warns inflation risks remain
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA has acknowledged its rate hikes are having an effect on the economy, but today's inflation data shows the job isn't done yet. In a speech published this week, the RBA flagged it is moving toward a 'demand-driven liquidity regime' — essentially a more flexible approach to managing money in the banking system. The bottom line for everyday Australians: don't expect rate cuts anytime soon, and today's inflation read makes another hike more likely before any relief arrives.

ai.summary: Big hardware news from Apple today with new M6 chips packing serious AI compute power. Meanwhile, Perplexity and Nvidia have teamed up on a local AI device, OpenAI is calling for more regulation after its own cybersecurity scare, and AI governance debates are heating up globally.

stories.title: Apple unveils M6 and M5 Ultra chips — a major leap in AI performance
stories.why_it_matters: Apple officially announced its new M6 and M5 Ultra chips today, touting them as a 'big leap in performance and AI compute.' The M6 is expected to power the next generation of Macs and potentially iPhones, with significantly faster on-device AI processing — meaning things like real-time translation, image generation, and Siri improvements happen on your device without sending data to the cloud. Apple also announced a refreshed Mac Mini featuring M6 and M5 Pro options. This keeps Apple competitive with the AI chip arms race being led by Nvidia.

stories.title: Perplexity and Nvidia launch 'Portable Computer' — a fully local AI agent with no ongoing costs
stories.why_it_matters: Perplexity AI (the AI search engine) has partnered with Nvidia to launch a 'Portable Computer' — a physical device that runs AI entirely on your local hardware, with zero 'token costs' (no per-use fees like you'd pay with ChatGPT). The device uses Nvidia chips and acts as a fully local AI agent, meaning it can answer questions, run tasks, and process information without sending anything to the internet. This is a big deal for privacy-conscious users and could eventually undercut the subscription model of cloud AI services.

stories.title: OpenAI calls for more AI regulation after its own cybersecurity hack reveals AI's hacking power
stories.why_it_matters: In an awkward twist, OpenAI — maker of ChatGPT — suffered a cybersecurity incident that demonstrated just how effective AI can be at hacking. The company has since called for stricter government regulation of AI, including in cybersecurity. The incident highlighted a growing concern: the same AI tools that help businesses and consumers can be weaponised by bad actors. OpenAI asking for regulation it will also have to comply with is a notable shift — it suggests even the big AI labs are getting nervous about what they've built.

stories.title: AI governance debate heats up: Federal vs state rules, and global patchwork approaches
stories.source: The Regulatory Review / Tech Policy Press
stories.why_it_matters: Two separate pieces today highlight the messy global battle over how to regulate AI. In the US, there's a fight between federal and state governments over who gets to set the rules — with tech companies lobbying hard to prevent a fragmented patchwork of 50 different state laws. Meanwhile, Colombia is reportedly drafting an AI law described as 'a poor copy' of Europe's AI Act. The lack of consistent international standards creates real uncertainty for AI companies — including the ones in your portfolio like Google and Microsoft.

sport.summary: NRL Round 26 kicks off Thursday night at Suncorp with Broncos v Storm. AFL All-Australian team was unveiled with Nick Daicos dominating, and there's a moving story from this week's AFL awards night.

stories.title: NRL Power Rankings: Roosters lose top spot, Bunnies on the brink, Titans hit rock bottom
stories.why_it_matters: After Round 25, Zero Tackle's power rankings show the Sydney Roosters have slipped off the top spot. South Sydney Rabbitohs are described as 'on the brink' — putting serious pressure on them heading into this weekend's clash against the Gold Coast Titans, who themselves have hit rock bottom of the rankings. For Gold Coast fans, the Titans' form is a major concern with finals spots starting to crystallise.

stories.title: Round 26 preview: Everything you need to know, tips and lineups
stories.why_it_matters: Round 26 of the NRL season is locked and loaded. Thursday night's blockbuster at Suncorp Stadium has the Brisbane Broncos hosting Melbourne Storm — a must-watch for Gold Coast fans given the Broncos are local rivals and the Storm are always finals contenders. The Cowboys v Wests Tigers on Saturday night should be comfortable for North Queensland, while the Warriors host the Knights in Auckland on Sunday. Full lineups are confirmed and available via Sporting News.

stories.title: AFL All-Australian team unveiled — Nick Daicos dominates awards night
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's prestigious All-Australian team was unveiled this week, with Collingwood's Nick Daicos dominating the awards. The All-Australian team recognises the best players of the season across all clubs — Daicos's dominance confirms he's the standout player of the 2026 season and a strong Brownlow Medal favourite. The night also featured significant individual awards — full recap available at AFL.com.au.

stories.title: 'You are enough': AFL superstar delivers emotional speech in tribute to late brother
stories.why_it_matters: In one of the most emotional moments of this AFL season, a superstar player delivered a powerful speech at the All-Australian awards in tribute to their late brother, declaring 'you are enough' to a tearful audience. Fox Sports reports the speech had the AFL world in tears. No details on the player's identity were available in the headline alone, but it's been described as one of the most memorable moments of the 2026 AFL season — a reminder that there's far more to sport than what happens on the field.

stories.title: GTA 6 leaks keep coming — and Take-Two lawyers reportedly turned up at a leaker's home
stories.why_it_matters: A massive 'Cyberleaks' episode is unfolding around GTA 6, with a wave of new content — gameplay footage, map details, and story elements — leaking online ahead of the game's release. Things escalated dramatically when a player who reportedly predicted the leaks claimed Take-Two and Rockstar Games sent lawyers to his home to identify the source. The LA Times has a full breakdown of what's been leaked. For Take-Two (TTWO) investors, the leaks create some short-term noise but historically pre-release hype — even from leaks — tends to drive massive launch sales.
